title: SOLARIS REPAIR 01 — five Solaris tools made reachable, honestly tested, and repaired
head: 9187f38
status_rationale: M1-M5 all landed with live oracles on Houdini 22.0.368. Two independent crucible passes; the first returned NO-GO and was looped back before any receipt was written. Status is green because every milestone's oracle was met and independently reproduced — not because nothing is left; the residuals are real and enumerated.

for_ruling.title: The suite count has three producers and no agreement
for_ruling.detail: 4744 passed / 100 skipped (feat/cto-relay-01, system 3.14.2, regenerated twice with a command line); 4841→4873 passed (feat/solaris-repair-01, system 3.14.2, WITH the pythonpath fix); 4891 collected under hython3.13 in the worktree vs 4790 in the primary checkout. Three different roots, unreconciled. Law 2 says every number names its producer — these now do, but they still disagree, and no governing document says which is canonical.
for_ruling.ask: Which tree and which interpreter defines the SYNAPSE suite baseline? Until that is ruled, `harness/verify/suite_baseline.json` pins a number whose meaning depends on where you stand.

for_ruling.title: The worktree pythonpath defect is almost certainly not SR1-only
for_ruling.detail: Every git worktree in this repo silently tests the PRIMARY checkout via the editable .pth at C:\Users\User\Synapse\python. I fixed it in pyproject on this branch only. Any prior leg that ran a suite from a worktree and reported green may have been verifying a different tree — including baselines now treated as floors.
for_ruling.ask: Should the pythonpath fix be promoted to master ahead of Gate C, and should previously-banked worktree suite evidence be re-qualified?

for_ruling.title: Schemas are Law-1 decorations across the Solaris family
for_ruling.detail: schema_*.py files have ZERO consumers (grep TOOL_RETURN outside the schema files finds none). The set_purpose enum drifted from [set, already_set, not_found] to code returning set|updated|unchanged|noop|not_found and nothing failed. M5 added test_schema_matches_implementation_contract for the parameter side only.
for_ruling.ask: Either wire the schemas to something that can fail, or delete them. A schema nothing validates against is the exact defect class this leg exists to remove.

for_ruling.title: F4 was repaired before it was verified to be a defect
for_ruling.detail: The BATON named F4 as HIGH with a specific mechanism. That mechanism is REFUTED-LIVE on 22.0.368. A fix was written, shipped with a green test, and the test could not fail. It took adversarial mutation testing to catch. The finding that produced F4 (harness/notes/l2_wiring_findings.md) asserted host behaviour that was never probed.
for_ruling.ask: Should F1-F11 as a set be re-qualified against the live build before any further work cites them? At least one of eleven was a phantom defect.

for_ruling.title: git push is structurally denied — correctly — and that blocked an explicitly approved act
for_ruling.detail: Joe approved pushing feat/cto-relay-01 and archive/root-scratch-2026-07-25 in writing. harness/relay-settings.json denies `git push`, and Article I's corollary rules that a ruling item, not something to route around. The agent refused, did not touch the settings file, and wrote C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE\.claude\remediation_ticket.md. Nothing was pushed. Docs landed at 1d3ac69 and d9b8aa3 on feat/cto-relay-01, unpushed.
for_ruling.ask: Joe runs the two push lines himself, OR a dispatch is issued under a profile that grants push. The fence held; it needs a human to open it.

for_ruling.title: Gate 0.1b is decided by evidence, but the gate itself is Gate A
for_ruling.detail: The one crash blocking 0.1b is Qt-side and residency-triggered, not the vendored tree. The vendor tree is ACTIVE and imports clean on hython3.13. See out_of_band above and harness/notes/GATE_01B_TRACE.md.
for_ruling.ask: Gate A (sidecar vs abi3) is never automated. The evidence now points away from abi3 being the blocker. Joe's call.

for_ruling.detail: Ruling 23 and R17 carry 136 and 1,506 LOC respectively; `find python/synapse/panel/providers -name '*.py' | xargs wc -l` reports 1,510 on feat/cto-relay-01.
